scope: Read-only analysis of aggregate JSON and retained StableHLO/optimized HLO. No execution, new test, download, source/math/threshold/LR edit or hardware operation.

fixed_boundary_stitch_controls.definition: Every variant tail receives the fixed captured named r and every variant prefix receives the fixed captured named ct_r. These are not each variant's own composed-chain intermediates/cotangents. Differences against full conflate fixed-boundary operand substitution, dtype and fusion/materialization; this is not a pure fusion test.

concrete_optimized_hlo_difference.boundary: BF16 query scale VJP followed by inverse RoPE, before Q-projection backward GEMMs.
concrete_optimized_hlo_difference.scale: Both use the same BF16-rounded1/sqrt128 =0.08837890625; neither a different source scale nor a precision-enum mismatch was found.

stablehlo_source_order.fact: Both StableHLO source graphs first multiply raw Splash dQ by BF16 scale, then inverse-RoPE sin/cos products. Named uses grouped Hkv×Hq_per_group axes; native flat Hq plus explicit sharding constraints.

named_prefix_optimized.sequence: BF16 dQscaled=roundBF16(dQraw*scale); inverse-RoPE uses separately rounded BF16(dQscaled*cos) and BF16(dQscaled*sin).

native_prefix_optimized.sequence: Precompute cosScaled=roundBF16(cos*scale),sinScaled=roundBF16(sin*scale). Multiply raw Splash dQ directly by these scaled coefficients, round products BF16, then combine inverse rotation.

concrete_optimized_hlo_difference.interpretation: These are distinct BF16 rounding sequences after optimization, while being equal over real arithmetic. Head64 previous attention replay had power-of-two scale1/8; head128 now has a non-power-of-two BF16 scale. That prior result did not test this noncommuting rounding case.
concrete_optimized_hlo_difference.limits: Raw Splash dQ, its input/residual arguments, scaled dQ and inverse-RoPE outputs were not saved. Matching kernel code does not prove equal runtime kernel operands/outputs. Therefore the HLO difference is an evidence-backed candidate, not yet a proven explanation of the numerical magnitude or a classified compiler defect.

reference_interpretation.reference: Actual native modules and same Splash backend at FP32 highest, with captured BF16 x/cotangent cast to FP32 and common FP32 masters. It changes compute dtype and fusion as well as precision; it is a diagnostic reference, not exact real arithmetic or a native-vs-named FP32 comparison.
reference_interpretation.finding: Both BF16 paths show ordinary dtype/precision-sensitive discrepancies against FP32. Neither is uniformly closer: full Q error is about0.9254% named vs0.9277% native. This does not exonerate or identify the particular scale/RoPE reassociation.

conclusions: The previously invalid duplicate-full capture context has been removed. All retained exact source/normal forward/loss/source-hash controls and33full/composed values pass; this validates the stated common-operand replay boundaries only.
Tail named/native forward,input VJP and4active parameter VJPs are exact (all11returned entries exact;5attention/inputnorm parameter entries are unused zero gradients).

Attention prefix already contains persistent Q-master and input-VJP differences. In both BF16 variants their actual output hashes match full replay exactly; this is stronger than matching cross-variant statistics.

Inputnorm gradients change when isolated from full to fixed-boundary prefix in both implementations. Additional full replay down/K/V discrepancies and absence of the normal full-Trainer up/O discrepancies prove fusion context still changes some gradient details.
No production patch, numerical acceptance or performance/convergence claim is warranted from this diagnostic alone.
